subject.title: Agents/tool-images: memoize resize to avoid per-turn sharp decode (#64418)

question: Should sanitized image resize results be retained in one bounded process-wide cache across agents and sessions, or must the cache lifetime follow an agent/session replay lifecycle?
rationale: Source, tests, and proof establish the memoization behavior, but they cannot establish maintainer intent for retaining session-derived image content after the originating session becomes inactive.

options.title: Scope cache to agent/session
options.body: Own and discard the cache with the agent or replay lifecycle while preserving the current keying, byte bound, and tests.

options.title: Accept process-wide cache
options.body: Keep the fixed 64 MiB module cache and explicitly accept cross-session in-process retention until eviction or restart.

recommendation.title: Scope cache to agent/session
recommendation.body: Own and discard the cache with the agent or replay lifecycle while preserving the current keying, byte bound, and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history and review signals are concentrated in the exact sanitizer and replay path affected by this lifecycle choice.
